# Table header buttons drop the scope an up. renderer resolved, unlike grid columns

## Context

Agreed with @neo-opus-grace as the table-side follow-up to #18771 / PR #18773 (approved). Once #18773 merges, grid and table give a column's `up.name` renderer a different `this`:

| | `up.name` renderer runs on |
|---|---|
| grid, after #18773 | the ancestor that defines the method — `grid.column.Base#beforeSetRenderer` records the scope `resolveCallback` resolved |
| table, on `dev` | `tableContainer` — `table/header/Button#beforeSetRenderer` keeps `.fn` only, and `table/Body.mjs:173`/`:175` default to the container |

A column config that works in one sibling silently changes `this` in the other.

## The Problem

`src/table/header/Button.mjs:227`:

```js
beforeSetRenderer(value, oldValue) {
    return resolveCallback(value, this).fn
}
```

`resolveCallback` returns `{fn, scope}`; for `up.name` the scope is the instance that defines the method, and it is dropped. `table/Body#applyRendererOutput` then calls `column.renderer.call(column.rendererScope || tableContainer, …)`.

**One shipped example is written against the table's current rule.** `examples/table/nestedRecordFields/Viewport.mjs#editRenderer` is defined on the Viewport, reached through `renderer: 'up.editRenderer'`, and does `me.body.updateDepth = -1`. The Viewport has no `body`; `table.Container` does. It works only because the renderer runs with `this = tableContainer`, and it already receives `tableContainer` as an argument. The other two table `up.` renderers (`countryRenderer` in `examples/table/cellEditing` and `nestedRecordFields`) call `this.getStateProvider()`, which resolves to the same provider from either instance.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/table/header/Button.mjs:88` — `renderer_: 'cellRenderer'`; `:242` `cellRenderer(data)` returns `data.value` and never reads `this`.
- `src/table/Body.mjs:173` — `bindCallback(column.renderer, …)` only acts on a renderer that is still a string, so it does not interfere once `beforeSetRenderer` has resolved a function.
- Census at `origin/dev`: no class in `src/`, `apps/` or `examples/` imports `table/header/Button` to subclass it, and no table consumer sets `rendererScope`.
- A plain name resolves against a view controller that defines it, else the column (`util/Function.mjs#resolveCallback`, `controller/Component#getHandlerScope`), so the rule moves plain names off the Container too. No table consumer is affected: `table.Container#createColumns` turns names of its own methods into functions before the column exists, and the census above finds no subclass.

## The Fix

- `table/header/Button#beforeSetRenderer` adopts #18773's rule: when `value` is a string that resolved, and `rendererScope` is unset, record the resolved scope. A function renderer keeps the `tableContainer` default.
- `examples/table/nestedRecordFields/Viewport.mjs#editRenderer` reads `tableContainer.body` instead of `me.body` — scope-independent, and correct under both rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — a table column's `up.name` renderer runs on the ancestor that defines it. Red-first on `dev`.
- [ ] **AC-2** — a function renderer without `rendererScope` still runs on `tableContainer`, and an explicit `rendererScope` still wins.
- [ ] **AC-3** — `examples/table/nestedRecordFields` still renders its Edit buttons, witnessed rather than assumed (the example has no arm today).
- [ ] **AC-4** — the table unit and component collections stay green.

## Out of Scope

- `rendererScope: 'me' | 'this'` for tables — `grid/Row.mjs` maps those strings to the column, `table/Body.mjs` does not; no table consumer uses them. Worth its own note, not this leaf.
- The unused `scope` local at `table/Body.mjs:672`.
- Changing #18773.

## Related

- #18771 / PR #18773 — the grid rule this adopts. #6620 — the original grid scope fix.
